Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

other adjective and pronoun

not this one; other people

also others, other people, other things, other than, other people’s

classical

Hor. S. 2.4.21: aliīs male crēditur
Ov. Ars 3.121: prīsca juvent aliōs

alius, alia, aliud

adjective and pronoun; dat. aliī; for the genitive alterīus is usual

other; in the plural, others, other things

Other people are aliī, other things alia. “Other than” is alius nisi or alius ac: ab aliō nisi ab rēge (Gell. 5.2.3). The rest of a group already named are cēterī (see the others); of two, alter (see the other).

Other words

  • aliēnus, aliēna, aliēnum — other people’s, someone else’s

    adjective · also used · classical · Publil. Sent. A 28: Aliēna nōbīs, nostra plūs aliīs placent.

    Belonging to another, as against suus and noster: aliēna, other people’s things.

Examples

  • prātēnsibus optima fungīs nātūra est; aliīs male crēditur

    meadow mushrooms are the best by nature; the other kinds are not to be trustedHor. S. 2.4.20–21

  • prīsca juvent aliōs: ego mē nunc dēnique nātum grātulor

    let the old days please others: I am glad I was born nowOv. Ars 3.121–122

  • Aliēna nōbīs, nostra plūs aliīs placent.

    Other people’s things please us, and ours please others more.Publil. Sent. A 28

  • haud umquam īnscendī sēsē ab aliō nisi ab rēge passus sit

    he never let anyone other than the king mount himGell. 5.2.3

  • olīvae betācei cucurbitae bulbī, alia mīlle nōn minus lauta

    olives, beets, gourds, onions, a thousand other things no less finePlin. Ep. 1.15.2

  • hāc rē vidēre nostra mala nōn possumus; aliī simul dēlinquunt, cēnsōrēs sumus

    that is why we cannot see our own faults; as soon as others go wrong, we are their censorsPhaedr. 4.10.4–5

See also another, the others, the other, different, else.

SourcesLewis & Short: alius · Lewis & Short: alienus

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-horatius, loci-ovidius, loci-publilius, loci-gellius, loci-plinius, loci-phaedrus), checked against the editions named there.

Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s.
